decision: Metal wires a bound buffer in full on first use: binding a 4.6 GB mmapped shard with setBuffer alone raised the system wired count by 4.8 GB in 60 ms whatever the kernel read, and task_info footprint and resident_size did not move; the CPU page walk moved resident_size, not wired
why: the memory saving of a mode is the sum of the buffers it binds, so quantized modes must not bind the whole shards; the metric to report is the wired delta from host_statistics64, with task_info beside it
evidence: scratchpad wire_probe.swift output in the transcript (12:3x); vm_stat Pages wired down 464494 before, 748907 after
result: design: quantized modes bind the cache file plus page-aligned sub-buffers over the in-place tensors they still read

decision: Formats: int8 per row with fp16 scales in groups of 128 along K; int4 in groups of 64 with an fp16 scale and fp16 bias (w = s*q + b); experts re-quantized FP8 to the same int4; the router and the N<=256 projections stay bf16 in every mode; lm_head stored as its 4097 candidate rows; embeddings stay in place; small vectors are copied into the cache file; balanced keeps FP8 experts in place through sub-buffers over each layer's contiguous expert runs
why: fp16 scale error 2^-11 is an eighth of the int8 step at half the bytes of fp32; group 64 int4 costs 4.5 bits per weight against 5 for group 32 and decode is bandwidth bound; the narrow matrices are 1 percent of the bytes and gate routing and the recurrence; the shard scan showed each layer's experts in 2 to 4 contiguous runs
evidence: scratchpad/brief.md; scratchpad/shard_layout.py output in the transcript
